title: Rh factor in pregnancy
body: Meena, whose blood group is O Rh negative, has just delivered her first baby. The baby is healthy and its blood group is found to be O Rh positive, like the father's. During the pregnancy the placenta kept the blood of mother and foetus well separated, but at delivery a small amount of the baby's blood may have entered Meena's circulation. The doctor explains that this exposure can make Meena's body start producing antibodies against the Rh antigen. If her next foetus is also Rh positive, these antibodies could leak into the foetal blood and destroy its red blood cells, a condition that may cause severe anaemia and jaundice in the baby or even be fatal.

title: Comparing two hearts
body: In a physiology activity, two volunteers were monitored at rest. Volunteer X, a student, had a heart rate of 75 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 mL. Volunteer Y, a trained athlete, had a resting heart rate of 50 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 100 mL. The teacher reminded the class that stroke volume is the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle during one cardiac cycle, and that the body can alter both stroke volume and heart rate.
